title: Alert
description: A public warning or notice issued by a government: an emergency, an evacuation, a boil-water notice, a road closure. Modelled on the Common Alerting Protocol (OASIS CAP 1.2), the international standard behind IPAWS in the US, EU-Alert, and national warning systems worldwide. schema.org has SpecialAnnouncement, but every one of its properties is COVID-shaped - quarantineGuidelines, gettingTestedInfo, travelBans - and it carries no severity, urgency, certainty, or expiry, so it is used only as a discovery projection, never as the model. Alerts are outbound (government to public); service requests are inbound. The two are deliberately separate profiles.

sender.description: The GovernmentOrganization issuing. Required: an unattributed warning cannot be trusted or verified.

sent.description: CAP sent. Full date-time with offset.

alertStatus.description: CAP status. 'exercise' and 'test' must never be rendered to the public as real; publishing them without this field is dangerous.

messageType.description: CAP msgType. An update or cancel must carry 'references' so consumers can supersede the earlier message rather than showing both.

references.description: Earlier alerts this supersedes, as resolvable references. Where the superseded alert is outside the published window, use referencesIdentifier instead.

referencesIdentifier.description: CAP identifiers of superseded alerts that are not present in this dataset. Real alert feeds are windowed: an update commonly supersedes an alert that has already expired out of the active feed. Requiring a resolvable reference would force a publisher to downgrade the update to a plain alert, which turns 'this supersedes an earlier warning' into 'this is a new warning' - materially wrong for a warning system. An update or cancel must carry references OR referencesIdentifier.

incident.description: CAP incidents: groups alerts about the same event.

note.description: CAP note: free-text context that doesn't fit another field.

alertInfo.description: CAP info blocks. One per language: CAP's alert/info split exists precisely so a warning can be issued in several languages at once, which matters wherever government operates multilingually.

event.description: Short event type, e.g. 'Boil water notice'.

instruction.description: What the public should do. The field that makes an alert actionable rather than merely informative.

expires.description: When the alert ceases to apply. Required: an alert with no expiry stays on screens indefinitely and trains people to ignore alerts.

area.description: Where the alert applies. Geometry is referenced, never embedded: a warning polygon is thousands of coordinate pairs and inlining it makes the alert unusable on the constrained channels alerts actually travel over.

areaDescription.description: Human-readable, e.g. 'North of the river, west of Route 9'.

geometry.description: Where the alert applies. A URL to a GeoJSON resource, or an inline Geometry for a small warning polygon. Inline is permitted because real CAP publishers embed the polygon in the alert itself - the NWS feed does - and a profile that only allowed references could not describe them.

geocode.description: Scheme-qualified area codes, e.g. SAME or UGC in the US.

sourceDataset.description: The `Dataset` this record was published as part of.
